headline: Brazilian Real Falls 14% Since October in Worst Emerging Market Performance
summary: Brazil's real fell 13.9 per cent against the US dollar between October 23 and November 16, marking the worst performance among 20 major currencies amid fiscal concerns.
why: Sharp currency depreciations increase imported inflation pressures, elevate foreign-denominated debt servicing costs, and prompt central bank currency interventions.

impacts.name: Brazilian Real
impacts.why: Fiscal concerns and market pressures drive significant depreciation of the currency against the US dollar.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Persistent fiscal worries and shifting economic forecasts prompted aggressive selling of the Brazilian real against major currencies.
